These claimed counts reproduced at cb096fb in a scratch archive: tests/g/jobs 46 (with the mutants file ignored), tests/g 486 (with the four mutant files ignored), the G3 list 74 passed under INFRX_MUTANTS=all (68 declared + 6), and --list '68 mutants over 42 named cases'. The code matches the commit claims. 5c157a2 identity_digest folds only async, and Ingress.validated uses it; POST /v1/jobs goes through _as_async, so chat+Prefer and POST /v1/jobs share one digest. My probes confirm the R94 behaviour on fakes. POST /v1/jobs k, then chat with no Prefer under k: 409 with lookup +1, admit unchanged, no staged/held/outbox write, and the async job completes (legacy; CREDIT is 409 with no write). Chat sync k, then POST /v1/jobs or chat+Prefer under k: 409 with no admit. Chat+Prefer k, then POST /v1/jobs k: 202 replayed, same handle. Stream vs sync under one key: 409 both ways, by payload. Same-mode sync and stream replays: 200 replayed with no admit. Terminal replay via chat+Prefer with a refusing host (legacy): 202 succeeded, 0 fetches, no writes. CREDIT replay deadline_at: one value over 6 retries.

The PostgreSQL 0011_admission.sql compares the stored mapping hash to p_idem payload_hash only. It never compares it to request.payload_digest, so 'PostgreSQL needs no change' holds for the conflict itself.

Two places where the evidence departs from what I observed. (1) The merge section's in-flight re-prepare text ('content-addressed and idempotent') omits that a failed re-prepare or recheck answers 400 for, or cancels, a live billable job. This is the known G2-confirm B1/B2, reproduced on the 202 path. (2) The R94 'before any store write' holds on fakes, but no test pins it, and it does not hold on PgJobStore until D5. These are omissions, not invented results.

votes.reason:
I reproduced both scenarios at cb096fb, so the finding stands and is blocking. In relay.py, Relay.admit runs prepare_request and stage whenever `found is None or found[1] is None`, and it runs `_admitted` (the card recheck, the capability check and attach) on that same condition. A job that is mapped and still in flight therefore gets fetched again and checked again on every same-key replay. `_admitted` handles a DomainError by calling `self.cancel(...)`, and a cancelled job is still a live job whose lease may be running.

To test it I added a temporary test file under tests/g/jobs that used the existing JobsWorld and test_jobs helpers. I deleted it after the run and `git status` is clean. Results:
(1) Legacy: POST /v1/jobs with a video and key=v returned 202. After `world.lease()` the fetcher answered 403. The same-key POST returned (400, 'media_fetch_failed'), with job.outcome None and the hold still held. The client gets a definitive invalid_request for a job that goes on running and billing.
(2) CREDIT: POST key=c, lease, commit 'Two' ' people', then set `relay.active_rate_card_version='rc_rotated_since'`. The same-key POST returned (400, 'invalid_request'), and the running job ended cancelled/client_cancelled with settlement_state held_unknown and reconcile_after set.

No G3 case covers this. The lost-202 test uses a healthy host and a healthy card. The terminal-replay test covers only a settled job, and the crash-after-commit test covers only an unattached job. The G3 evidence (G3-9e3bc71.md, the scope section) calls the in-flight re-prepare 'content-addressed and idempotent'. It does not disclose that a failed fetch or recheck becomes the answer, or that it cancels the running job.

This is a money and detach hole on the 202 path G3 introduces: a replay can cancel a billable running job and leave its settlement held_unknown, and a live job can be reported to the client as a 400. That makes it blocking. The fix belongs to G2 round 3 (the inherited G2-confirm B1/B2). G3 has to re-merge that head, add the two POST /v1/jobs cases and the mutants, and correct the evidence line.

I could not refute it; both scenarios reproduce at cb096fb. In Relay.admit (relay.py:152-160), prepare_request and stage run whenever found is None or found[1] is None. So a mapped job that is still in flight gets its media re-fetched. _admitted (186-189) also re-runs the CREDIT card and capability rechecks, and any DomainError makes it call self.cancel(..., client_cancelled).

I ran a scratch copy of the codex-g3 apps/infrx-api (the worktree was not modified) against its .venv, using the tests/g/jobs JobsWorld fakes.

(1) Legacy: POST /v1/jobs key=v with rs.VIDEO gives 202. world.lease() starts the job. The fetcher then answers 403. The same-key POST /v1/jobs returns 400 invalid_request_error media_fetch_failed after 1 fetch, while the job is running with its hold held. After world.complete the job is succeeded and settled, so it bills even though the client was told the request was invalid.

(2) CREDIT: POST key=c, then lease, then commit("a","b"), then active_rate_card_version='rc_rotated_since'. The same-key POST returns 400 invalid_request, and the running job is now cancelled/client_cancelled with settlement_state held_unknown and reconcile_after set.

No G3 case covers an in-flight replay whose re-prepare or recheck fails. The existing cases cover a lost 202 with a healthy host, a terminal replay with a 403, and a crash after commit with no refs attached. The evidence G3-9e3bc71.md:556 calls the re-fetch 'content-addressed and idempotent' and does not say a failure there becomes the answer. This is the same defect as G2-confirm-a786af7 B1/B2 (fix_required), now reachable through G3's 202 path. A retry can cancel a running billed CREDIT job, and a legacy retry gets a definitive 400 for a job that goes on to bill. That is a money hole, so G3 cannot close until it re-merges G2 round 3's fix and adds the two POST /v1/jobs cases.

votes.reason:
The mechanism is real, but the finding is not blocking.

I tested it on a scratch copy of cb096fb. I added `except errors.IdempotencyConflict: return None` to `relay._lookup` (apps/infrx-api/infrx/gateway/routes/relay.py:193-208). All of tests/g outside the mutant runner still passed: 531 passed, 14 deselected. So the mutant does survive. The mode-conflict 409 now comes from admit's `_replay`, after prepare and stage. MODES_409 checks only the status, one job and one hold.

It is not an R94 hole. R94 (08-contracts-v1-encoding.md:254) says the mode goes into the digest "so `lookup`/`admit` see the conflict before any store write; the fakes and PostgreSQL need no change". Under the mutant, admit still refuses before any JobStore write: no job, no hold, no attached wait, and the async job runs on. `mode_left_out_of_the_digest` kills a break of that invariant.

The property that goes untested is R91's: a conflicting key is refused before preparation, so no media is fetched and nothing is staged. R91 comes from G2, not G3:
- `_lookup` was written in G2 commits 21e7b03 and 367acc3, and G3 round 2 did not change it.
- The same gap already exists for a changed payload. `test_dur_admit__a_changed_payload_under_the_key_is_409_and_admits_nothing` does not count prepare or stage either.
- The PostgreSQL ordering (prepare and stage before the 409 until D5) is R91's recorded interim, a PENDING line naming D5. The `_lookup` docstring also records it ("ponytail: interim, D5 lifts it").

What a 409 costs under the mutant is one extra media fetch and one orphan staged payload. No money moves, no tenant is exposed and no job is detached. It also closes no round-1 item and causes no regression.

Worth doing as a follow-up: assert the lookup/admit call counts and the staged count across both 409s (payload and mode), add a `lookup_conflict_swallowed` mutant, and add a line in the G3 Limits noting that on PgJobStore the conflict comes after prepare/stage until D5.

The gap is real, but it doesn't block. Test: I copied cb096fb to a scratch directory and added `except errors.IdempotencyConflict: return None` to `Relay._lookup` in apps/infrx-api/infrx/gateway/routes/relay.py. All of tests/g still passed (545 passed). No test kills a 409 that arrives only after prepare and stage.

Why it doesn't block:
(1) R94's substance is tested, and the mode_left_out_of_the_digest mutant kills it. R94 puts the mode into the idempotency identity. A sync retry is 409 with no wait attached. The async job keeps running with one job and one hold, and the reverse direction is also 409. Under the swallowed-lookup mutant, what the client sees and the store holds is the same: 409, one job, one hold, and the job completes.
(2) The only extra effect is a wasted media fetch plus an orphaned staged payload object. No money, tenant or detach state is involved, because admit's replay check still refuses before any JobStore write.
(3) "The conflict is answered at lookup, before preparation" comes from R91 (08-contracts-v1-encoding.md: "a changed payload digest is the same conflict admit raises"), not from round 2. The same gap was already in the G2/R91 test test_dur_admit__a_changed_payload_under_the_key_is_409_and_admits_nothing, which also checks only the status, the job and the hold. The new MODES_409 test follows that existing pattern, so this is not a round-1 item left open and not a regression.
(4) On PostgreSQL, conflicts arriving after prepare and stage is R91's interim, which R91 already records as PENDING until D5, and the `_lookup` docstring says so.

What is actually wrong:
- The evidence row claims "before any store write" (G3-9e3bc71.md:592), which overstates things. It is only true on the fakes and unpinned even there. Staging is a media-store write, and on PgJobStore the conflict follows prepare and stage until D5.
